gaps.term: elimination needs only row additions and swaps
gaps.quote: Gaussian elimination (reducing a matrix to $I$ by row operations) over $\mathbb F_2$ needs only row additions and row swaps.
gaps.note: The page does not say why row scaling is not needed (over F_2 the only nonzero scalar is 1) and gives no argument that elimination reaches I for every invertible matrix.

gaps.term: every invertible matrix is a product of row additions
gaps.quote: Every $M\in\mathrm{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ is a product of row additions.
gaps.note: The page does not derive this from the elimination. It needs the inverses of the elimination steps to be taken in reverse order and each row addition to be its own inverse over F_2, and neither is stated.
